summary: This version of the playlist app stores song titles in a PriorityQueue, which keeps whichever title ranks best by its ordering rule at the front. Iterating over the queue prints the titles in no particular order, but polling them out one at a time plays them alphabetically.

lines.code: PriorityQueue<String> titleQueue = new PriorityQueue<>(); // natural A–Z order
lines.text: No comparator is supplied, so the queue falls back to the natural ordering of its elements — for strings that means alphabetical. Chapter 8's later example replaces this with a rule based on energy level.
The offer method is the queue's way of adding an element; the insertion order does not decide position, the ordering rule does.
Iterating a PriorityQueue walks its internal storage, not its priority order, so do not be surprised when these four titles come out jumbled.

lines.code: String nextTitle = titleQueue.poll(); // removes smallest (A–Z) first
lines.text: Only poll enforces the ordering: it removes and returns the element that best matches the rule, which here is the title earliest in the alphabet.
Because each poll removes an element, testing isEmpty each time round drains the whole queue and stops cleanly instead of returning null off the end.
